ai.description: *Megophrys zunhebotoensis* is a medium-sized toad (SVL 45–55 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark lateral patches. It features prominent horn-like dermal projections on the eyelids and a distinct snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys zunhebotoensis* is best distinguished by its unique, distinctively elongated, horn-like dermal projection on each upper eyelid, which is longer than in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys zunhebotoensis* inhabits moist, subtropical evergreen forests in the hilly regions of Nagaland, typically found at elevations between 1,200 and 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: Megophrys zunhebotoensis is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter to ambush small invertebrates while avoiding detection by potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys zunhebotoensis* breeds in streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys zunhebotoensis* is endemic to the Zunheboto district of Nagaland in Northeast India, occurring at elevations between 1,200 and 1,800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Megophrys zunhebotoensis* consists of a single, short, low-pitched "tock" sound, typically emitted from leaf litter in moist forest habitats.
